checks.issue: A WORD REJOINED ACROSS A LINE BREAK, the first of three on this page. Line 2 ends จาตุรังคิเก สาวะกะสันนิ- with a hyphen and line 3 opens ปาเต,. The hyphen is typesetting, so the word is rejoined as สาวะกะสันนิปาเต and the hyphen dropped. The other two are วัฑฒะมานะ- / กัจฉายายะ at verse 14 and มาฆะปุณณะมีนักขัต- / ตะสะมายัง at verse 19.

THIS OFFERING IS NOT A VARIANT OF THE OTHER THREE — it is different text. Visākha (p66) and Aṭṭhamī (p68) both open ยะมัมหะ โข มะยัง ภะคะวันตัง and recite the Buddha, Dhamma and Saṅgha formulas at length. This one opens อัชชายัง and recounts the fourfold assembly and the Ovāda-pāṭimokkha instead. Only its closing petition, verses 24 to 28, runs parallel to theirs. So it must NOT be stubbed as a repeat, and its English is written fresh rather than copied from the earlier printings.

อัฑฒะเตระสานิ, four times in this chant, at verses 8, 17 and 23. Read at the standard body size rather than magnified, because the ฑ/ฒ pair here is unambiguous in this face. It is aḍḍhaterasāni — 'half of the thirteenth hundred', the traditional way of saying one thousand two hundred and fifty, which is the number of bhikkhus at the assembly. Glossed as the number in English rather than left literal.

เวฬุวะเน IS ฬ, NOT พ, AND THIS ONE CAN BE READ. The photo map records that these photographs cannot tell ฬ from พ at body-text size, and that stands as a general warning — but ฬ carries a tall ascender that พ does not, and at 4x on an isolated crop the ascender is plainly there and is the same height as the one on ฬ elsewhere on the page. The canonical reading agrees: Veḷuvana, the Bamboo Grove at Rājagaha. Recorded as ฬ on the strength of the ascender rather than of the canon, but flagged, because this is exactly the class of judgement the map says to distrust.

ปะฏิคคัณหาตุ IS BARE AGAIN — no mark over the ณ, read at 4x on an isolated crop. That is pages 68, 69, 70 and now 71 all bare against page 67's ปะฏิคคัณ์หาตุ. Four against one, on the same word in the same closing formula, so the question is now firmly whether this printer sets the mark at all rather than which of the two marks it is.

THE ENGLISH OF THIS WHOLE CHANT IS A WORKING TRANSLATION AND NEEDS YOUR EYE. The page prints no Thai translation anywhere, so there is nothing to check it against, hence english_unverified. Verses 21 to 23 are the least certain: the book's commas cut that sentence in three places that do not fall where the grammar does, so the English is spread across the three units and each one reads oddly on its own. Read them together.

NO CHANT NUMBER, no invitation, and no colophon. The book prints the centred title and goes straight into the passage, exactly as it did for the Visākha and Aṭṭhamī offerings, and the passage ends at สุขายะ. with the next title following. The title is THAI, not Pali, so title_pali is empty and title_roman carries the Paiboon+ romanisation.

NO FOOTNOTE ON THIS PAGE, which is worth saying because its two predecessors both had three. Pages 67 and 69 carry editorial notes keyed to ถูโป, กะโต and ถูปัง in the circumambulation passage — words this chant does not contain, since it is about the assembly rather than walking round a stūpa. The foot of this sheet was checked on its own crop: no rule, no note, clear paper.

checks.issue: SET IN TWO COLUMNS, AND THIS IS THE FIRST PAIRING. The left cell holds มาฆะนักขัตตะยุตตายะ and the right ปุณณายะปุณณะมายังโย, joined into this one verse. The same tests that settled pages 69 and 70 apply and agree: the left column carries no punctuation, and read across the rows give continuous sense — row 4 is viharanto rājagahe … giribbhaye, one clause across the gutter. Read down, the left column is five unfinished half-lines.

THE RIGHT CELL IS PRINTED AS ONE UNBROKEN RUN — ปุณณายะปุณณะมายังโย, with no space before โย. Its Visākha counterpart on page 67 prints วิสาขะปุณณะมายัง โย with a space, and the app holds it that way. Transliterated here as the run it is printed as, puṇṇāyapuṇṇamāyaṃyo, rather than spaced out to match the other chant. Verse 2's โคตะโมหะโข is the same case.

มาฆะทานัง WHERE THE SENSE WANTS มาคะธานัง. Read at 4x on an isolated crop: the second consonant is ฆ and the fourth is ท, so the word as printed is māghadānaṃ. The standard line is viharanto rājagahe māgadhānaṃ giribbhaye — 'of the MAGADHANS', the people, which is what a hill-fort belongs to. It looks as though the compositor was pulled toward มาฆะ by the six other occurrences of it on this page. Reproduced exactly as printed and NOT corrected; the English gives the Magadhan sense, which is flagged here so the two do not silently disagree.

เวฬุวันนัมหิ with นน, where standard editions have veḷuvanamhi with one n. Read at 4x: there are clearly two น. The ฬ is certain here too — its ascender is visible at the same magnification. Reproduced as printed and transliterated veḷuvannamhi to match.

batch_status.notes: THREE CHANTS ON ONE SHEET — one closing, two opening — which is the fullest page in this stretch. Four things worth reading. (1) THE AṬṬHAMĪ SARAPHAÑÑA IS FINISHED at thirty verses, so stage 2 must REMOVE its CONTINUES marker; the new Māgha Saraphañña then opens its own. Its last line carries a full stop the app's Visākha twin does not, which is a FIFTH divergence between those two and the second that looks like a slip in the page-68 reading rather than a real difference. Nothing there was changed. (2) THE MĀGHA OFFERING IS NOT A VARIANT OF THE OTHER TWO. Visākha and Aṭṭhamī share almost every word; this one shares only its closing petition and is otherwise the story of the fourfold assembly. It is set in full and not stubbed. (3) TWO READINGS IN THE MĀGHA SARAPHAÑÑA DIFFER FROM THE CANON and both are reproduced: มาฆะทานัง where the sense wants มาคะธานัง, 'of the Magadhans', and เวฬุวันนัมหิ with a doubled น. The first is the one to look at — it reads like the compositor being pulled toward มาฆะ by the six other occurrences on the page. (4) ปะฏิคคัณหาตุ IS BARE FOR THE FOURTH PAGE RUNNING. Nothing on this page needs re-photographing.
